problem: The sentence "the first bit sets the starting level" is confusing and does not match the worked example, which needs a level before the first bit (+1 V) to produce any output at all. A student may think the first bit always determines the level in the same way.
fix: Say: the level before the first bit is a chosen reference (the example uses +1 V); a 1 then inverts that reference at the start of the bit, and a 0 leaves it unchanged.

problem: "RZ returns to 0 V in the second half of every bit. It gives a transition for every 1" describes unipolar RZ only. In polar RZ a 0 is sent as −V then 0 V, so every bit, 1 or 0, has a mid-bit transition. As written, a student will over-generalise the rule to all RZ.
fix: Label it unipolar RZ: "Unipolar RZ sends 1 as +V then 0 V and 0 as 0 V for the whole bit, so a transition appears only for a 1. Polar RZ sends 0 as −V then 0 V, so every bit has a mid-bit transition. Either form needs more bandwidth than NRZ."

problem: "No transition during a run of 0s" is incomplete: a run of 1s also gives no transition in unipolar NRZ, since the level stays at +V.
fix: "No transition during a long run of 0s or of 1s."

problem: The NRZ-I trace starts at −1 without saying why. The reader cannot tell that this comes from a chosen level of +1 V before the first bit, so the figure and the worked example seem to disagree on the starting point.
fix: Add to the caption: "NRZ-I assumes the level just before the first bit is +1 V, as in the worked example."
